source.title: Minor interpretability exploration #2: Extending superposition to different activation functions

page_placements.theme: Toy-model superposition geometry depends on sparsity, correlation, importance, loss, activation function and regularization

record.file_problem: The supplied post text is intact. It refers to external notebooks, graphs, and tables, whose contents are not included here.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies activation functions in a toy superposition model and reports that superposition changes substantially across functions, refining the claim that activation choice can affect polysemanticity. It does not test trained image or language models.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes for its own toy-model runs and an aggregate loss range. It also cites earlier findings about activation functions; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Linked graphs and tables are not available in the supplied text, so no values are extracted from them.
record.test_reason: The post reruns Anthropic's toy model of superposition with 26 activation functions in place of ReLU. It reports the 'degree of superposition' (features packed into a non-privileged hidden bottleneck) and loss, described only in words. It never measures neurons responding to unrelated inputs, nor any share of polysemantic neurons. Its measure is a related construct, not the behaviour any version names, so no row links to a version. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Readers who treat toy-model superposition as a proxy for V5 could read these rows as T3 evidence for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes more superposition gives marginally smaller losses. Non-negative, asymmetrical (and smooth) activation functions gave the most superposition and lowest losses. Loss and superposition are only loosely tied, so some superposition could be removed without much performance cost. The results are preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Anthropic toy model of superposition notebook and a reproduction/extension as its basis, replacing ReLU with other activation functions and extending sparsity regimes. This is a toy-model exploration, not a reproduction of the original neuron-level analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function and sparsity regime affect the reported superposition patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: In the toy superposition model, the degree of superposition varies strongly across activation functions while loss stays in a narrow 10^-4 to 10^-3 range. Tanh, Hardtanh and SELU showed little superposition, and SoLU less at high sparsity. LeakyReLU, GELU and Softplus showed the most; ReLU6 and ReLU^2 matched ReLU. Hardness generally slowed superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy models of superposition, the choice of activation function changes how much feature superposition develops, with only small effects on loss.

record.problems: The author characterizes the exploration as small, low-stakes, and without prior predictions. The supplied text gives mostly qualitative findings, no uncertainty estimates or explicit controls, and flags possible bugs or floating-point artifacts for some functions. The toy-model results do not establish effects in trained networks.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified per-activation results were included because the supplied post text provides no such numbers; the referenced graphs, tables, and notebooks are external. Cited findings from earlier work were excluded.

untested.parts: No share of polysemantic neurons in any model; only bottleneck superposition in a toy ReLU-output-style model. No architecture or regularization variation; no trained vision or language networks.

missing.what: Softmin showed an importance-reversing effect and LogSoftmax failed to converge. Exp and Exp linear behaved strangely and failed to converge at low sparsity. No row records these.

record.verdict_notes: I treated toy-model 'superposition' (features in a non-privileged bottleneck) as a different construct from neuron polysemanticity, so there are no verdicts. All values are qualitative; graphs and tables are in an external Drive folder. The 'Previous work' section cites Lad and Kostolansky (2023) findings, which should not be rows. The author flags possible bugs for the sigmoid-family results.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or InceptionV1 neurons are studied.
No transformer language models or language-model neurons are studied.
The study does not test whether superposition is caused by having more features than neurons.
Initialization, regularization, and training noise as causes of polysemanticity are not tested.

Tests activation-function variation in a toy superposition model only; it does not test modern convnets, other architectures, or regularization, nor does it report a quantified share of polysemantic neurons.
No canonical polysemantic neurons are examined for a shared feature or related jobs.
The study does not compare explanation methods or systematically vary which activation range is examined.

relation.reason: Its own experiments are on toy-model superposition, not neuron polysemanticity. It mentions polysemanticity only when citing prior work (Lad and Kostolansky). 'discusses' fits, and 'tests' does not.

tranche.reason: The post measures 'degree of superposition' in Anthropic's toy bottleneck model, where the swapped ReLU is the output nonlinearity, plus aggregate loss. It never measures neurons responding to unrelated inputs, so it fails V5's 'share of polysemantic neurons'. This is a related but different construct, and under verdict_rules section 1 that is not a test. It fits no version.

source_check.notes: Informal LessWrong post. All results are qualitative readings of graphs kept on Google Drive; the text gives no superposition numbers and does not define the measure. Superposition is measured in a toy bottleneck, not as polysemantic neurons, so it bears on V5 only by analogy. The post is also internally loose: GELU is called both 'less superposition over time' than ReLU and among 'the most superposition'.

statements.correction: Toy model of superposition, 26 activations besides ReLU; loss 10^-4 to 10^-3; (Hard)tanh and SELU very limited superposition; SoLU initially above ReLU, less as sparsity increased (with more low-level superposition).
statements.problem: none. Losses of 10^-4 to 10^-3, large superposition differences across activations, very limited superposition for (Hard)tanh/SELU, and less for SoLU as sparsity rose all match the text. Superposition is described only in words.
